source_refs.note: iv. Disinfection: a main subheading of 33.6 Wastewater Treatment, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 256-256.

blocks.text: Filtration alone cannot remove dissolved ions or microscopic pathogens; therefore, chemical purification is necessary. Chlorination is the most common method of disinfection. The other methods include sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl); ozone (O₃) or sometimes with hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂). When chlorine gas or sodium hypochlorite is added to water, it forms hypochlorous acid (HOCl), which penetrates the cell walls of bacteria and viruses, disrupting their cell functions.
